subject: fiqh
summary: Fiqh al-Sunnah by Shaykh Sayyid Sabiq (1915–2000 CE) is a comprehensive modern Islamic jurisprudence manual covering worship, transactions, and family law. Drawing directly on Quranic verses and authenticated hadith with references across all four major madhabs, it became one of the most widely read and accessible fiqh references in the twentieth century.
overview:
Fiqh al-Sunnah by the Egyptian scholar Shaykh Sayyid Sabiq (1915–2000 CE) is one of the most influential Islamic jurisprudence works of the twentieth century. Originally published in Egypt in the 1940s and 1950s, it was strongly encouraged by Imam Hasan al-Banna of the Muslim Brotherhood, under whose influence al-Sabiq had studied. The work was designed as a practical, hadith-referenced fiqh guide accessible to the educated Muslim layperson, bypassing the technical argumentation of classical madhab manuals.

Fiqh al-Sunnah covers the full range of Islamic personal and religious law: ritual purity, prayer, fasting, zakat, hajj, trade and commerce, marriage and divorce, inheritance, oaths, vows, and more. For each topic, al-Sabiq cites the relevant Quranic verses and hadith directly, notes the position of each of the four major madhabs where they differ, and typically indicates which position he considers most supported by evidence — without binding himself to a single school.

This comparative approach gave the book its enormous popularity among Muslims seeking to understand the reasoning behind rulings rather than simply following one school's conclusions. It was widely used in Islamic university curricula, particularly in Arab countries and among the new generation of Muslim scholars influenced by the hadith-focused revival movement.

Scholars have noted that some of al-Sabiq's hadith citations and authenticity assessments should be verified against later specialist scholarship — particularly the work of al-Albani and other twentieth-century muhaddithin. Several editions have been updated with additional commentary and authentication notes. The standard printed edition is in three volumes; Darussalam has published an English translation in five volumes. The work remains a highly useful accessible introduction to Islamic jurisprudence across all its major areas.
structure: 3 volumes; covers purity, prayer, fasting, zakat, hajj, transactions, and family law
